waterMl.notes: No change from FitPlate general water target. Prefer plain water and drinks without sugar; juice and sweet drinks do not count. Unusual thirst can signal high glucose: check glucose and talk to a doctor. Sick days, fasting and hot weather: ask the doctor for a sick-day plan.

conflictsWith.rule: P13 overrides protein: cap at 0.8 g/kg/day (KDIGO 2022) even if diabetes' 15-20% energy would be higher; sodium under 2000 mg/day; potassium and phosphorus limits only from the doctor; switch off potassium-based salt substitutes; requires_doctor_input stays true

Same direction: keep saturated fat under 7% energy and use LAI targets (LDL under 70 / non-HDL under 100 mg/dL; under 50 / under 80 if very high risk); favour pulses, nuts and fish over cream, ghee and red meat

Protein may rise to the P27 value only if there is no kidney disease (no eGFR under 60, no raised urine albumin, P13 not selected); otherwise the CKD cap applies. Surplus comes from protein and whole-food carbohydrate around workouts, not sugar or mass gainers. Show the hypoglycaemia note for insulin/sulfonylurea users

Pregnancy needs override diabetes weight-loss logic: no calorie deficit; glucose targets are stricter and set by the obstetric/diabetes team; the app shows only general guidance until the doctor confirms targets

Apply as a food filter: no root vegetables (removes potato, onion, garlic, carrot); protein from dals, besan, paneer, curd, milk, nuts and soya; millets and non-root vegetables for fibre; Paryushan and other fasts follow the diabetes fasting safety rules
Compatible; use a larger calorie deficit only if not on insulin/sulfonylurea or the doctor agrees
Compatible; use the stricter sodium limit of the two profiles

warnings: General information, not medical advice. The app does not diagnose or treat diabetes and never suggests changing or stopping medicines.

Insulin or sulfonylurea users: risk of low blood sugar with skipped meals, fasting, alcohol or hard exercise. Do not go below 45% energy from carbohydrate, use a large calorie deficit or follow a fasting plan without the doctor's agreement.
Low blood sugar (under 70 mg/dL): take 15 g fast-acting carbohydrate, recheck after 15 minutes, repeat if still low (ADA 15-15 rule). Under 54 mg/dL, confusion or fainting is an emergency.
Religious fasting (Navratri, Ekadashi, Ramadan, Paryushan): talk to the doctor beforehand; break the fast if glucose is under 70 mg/dL or very high (300 mg/dL or more).
Kidney disease, pregnancy, repeated or unnoticed lows: targets must be confirmed by a doctor.
Long-term metformin users: ask the doctor about periodic vitamin B12 testing, especially with numbness or tingling.
Potassium-based low-sodium salts are not for people with kidney disease or on certain BP medicines unless the doctor agrees.
